title: The Resolution of the Identity as a Generator of Exact Integral Identities: A Coherent-State Approach
abstract: The resolution of the identity is typically utilized as a passive representation tool in standard quantum mechanics textbooks. In this paper, we reinterpret this traditional perspective by introducing the resolution of the identity associated with Glauber coherent states as a direct generator of exact complex Gaussian integral identities. By systematically projecting the continuous coherent-state completeness relation onto the discrete Fock basis, highly generalized Gaussian integral relations emerge naturally as a direct consequence of state preservation, rather than being introduced as independent mathematical postulates. We demonstrate that this overarching formal structure simultaneously dictates both discrete (Kronecker delta) and continuous (Dirac delta) localization kernels under appropriate basis projections, providing a sharp conceptual contrast between the structural features of overcomplete and strictly orthogonal representations. Crucially, we highlight an intriguing non-commuting behavior in the parameter limits of the master identity. Requiring only the elementary properties of coherent states and the Dirac formalism, this approach offers a transparent and visually intuitive illustration of how Hilbert-space completeness inherently encodes vast libraries of exact, solvable mathematical relations -- providing a unifying perspective suitable for advanced undergraduate and graduate instruction.
summary: This work treats the Resolution of the Identity not as a given postulate but as an active generator for exact integral identities in quantum theory. By analyzing coherent states and projecting onto discrete bases, the authors show that the structure of state preservation dictates whether the resulting identity is a Kronecker delta or a Dirac delta. This offers a unifying perspective on basis representations across quantum mechanics.
main_problem: The paper reinterprets the Resolution of the Identity (ROI) from a passive mathematical tool into an active generator that dictates exact integral identities across different quantum bases.
main_result: It demonstrates that the structural consistency required by Hilbert space completeness naturally yields both discrete orthonormality (Kronecker delta) and continuous localization kernels (Dirac delta).
method: The core method involves systematically projecting the continuous coherent-state completeness relation onto the discrete Fock basis to derive integral representations for expansion coefficients.
model_or_system: The study is set in general separable Hilbert spaces, utilizing Glauber coherent states ($\alpha$), position eigenstates ($x$), and the discrete Fock basis ($n$).
key_observables: Overlap functions (e.g., $\langle eta|\alphaangle$, $\langle x'|xangle$) and resulting identity kernels ($\delta_{nm}$, $\delta(x-x')$).
important_parameters: The coherent state parameter $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ and the scaling parameter $\sigma$ used to transition between overcomplete and localized representations.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes a separable Hilbert space structure and relies on analyzing asymptotic limits ($\sigma 	o 0$) when recovering strictly orthogonal bases from coherent states.
figures_summary: Conceptually compares identity kernels, showing that overcomplete manifolds require an asymptotic contraction ($\sigma 	o 0$) to yield the sharp kernel seen in strictly orthogonal bases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the general formalism, then applying it specifically to coherent states (deriving a master integral identity and noting non-commutativity), followed by analyzing position eigenstates and Fock states separately before unifying these findings.
why_interesting: It provides a deep structural insight into quantum mechanics foundations, showing how seemingly independent mathematical postulates like orthonormality are unified under the single principle of Hilbert space completeness.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A conceptual comparison of identity kernels generated by the ROI framework. (a) In the overcomplete coherent-state manifold, individual states fundamentally overlap, and the Dirac delta distribution emerges only asymptotically as the continuous limit of a contracting Gaussian profile (σ →0). (b) In strictly orthogonal continuous (position) or discrete (Fock) bases, the localization kernels (δ-distribution or Kro- necker δnm) emerge directly and without any limiting process as an inherent requirement for geometric self-consistency.
